video.title: How to Start Reselling (Even With $0 in the Bank)

summary: Chris Koerner hosts Shannon Jean, a liquidation/auction reseller, who screen-shares live auction listings (Target, B-Stock, GovDeals, QVC, Costco, Advance Auto Parts) and explains how to buy pallets and truckloads at ~90-99% off nominal retail and resell locally on Facebook Marketplace, eBay or wholesale. Key rules: always get a manifest, buy with math and sell with emotion, list items before buying to test demand, focus on recovering your initial investment fast, buy seasonal and boring commodity goods, and buy close to home. Several side ideas are pitched (free couch flipping, Costco/IKEA arbitrage for towns without stores, Christmas tree lot, AI manifest analysis). Shannon sells a Reseller Mastermind and Koerner sells TK Owners, so claims are second-hand or promotional and many numbers are anecdotal.

speakers.name: Chris Koerner
speakers.description: Host of The Koerner Office; also shares his own Facebook Marketplace and Tesla credit experiments

speakers.name: Shannon Jean
speakers.description: Liquidation and auction reseller who runs a Reseller Mastermind and screen-shares live auctions

ideas.name: Liquidation pallet auction flipping on Facebook Marketplace
ideas.one_liner: Buy new overstock pallets from B-Stock and similar auctions at huge discounts to nominal retail, then resell locally on Facebook Marketplace.
ideas.customer: Local Facebook Marketplace buyers looking for cheap new goods (furniture, pools, docks, rugs, appliances)
ideas.problem: Shoppers want new items below retail; retailers must liquidate overstock
ideas.offer: Brand new, factory-sealed items (e.g. Walker Edison furniture, Target sporting goods) priced near used comparables

price_points.label: Rattan king bed conservative sale, landed cost about $30

pricing.notes: Price near used comparables on Facebook Marketplace; mention 'similar to IKEA' in listings.

acquisition_channels.details: List on Facebook Marketplace with own photos, assembly time-lapse video, and keywords; use stock photos, say brand new.

quote.text: you take some video of you building it, you do a time-lapse video of you putting it together. That should be the first media.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

acquisition_channels.details: Post in local Facebook groups such as parent and college groups.

ideas.delivery: Buyer wins pallet auction, pays freight (e.g. about $1,200 for 16 pallets in California), stores in garage or storage unit, assembles sample items, buyers collect locally.
unit_economics_claims: Target sporting goods lot cost per item $3.78 vs $250 retail
16 pallets Walker Edison furniture expected under $5,000 all in
Landed cost on rattan bed about $30 vs $350+ resale
ideas.startup_cost: Roughly $1,000 to $5,000 per lot plus freight; resale permit is free
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Days after pallet arrives; aim to recover investment fast

acquisition.how: Listings on Facebook Marketplace are inbound and can be drafted by agents, though FB posting has limited API support and needs human-in-the-loop.

onboarding.how: Buyer enquiries and pickup scheduling can be templated but need a human to coordinate.

delivery.how: Freight pickup, storage, assembly, photographing and handing over goods are physical.

billing.how: Mostly cash or app payments on pickup; little to automate.

support.how: Agents can handle pre-sale chat questions; returns are rare.

uk_applicability.notes: UK equivalents exist (B-Stock UK, Amazon/Argos liquidation pallets, Facebook Marketplace, eBay, Gumtree) but US resale permit rules do not apply and pallet freight and VAT differ.

risks: Inventory that does not sell must be donated
Dependence on weak or no manifest

quotes.text: Don't buy without a manifest. That is rule number what? Rule number one is don't buy unless you know what you can sell it for.
quotes.speaker: Shannon Jean

quotes.speaker: Shannon Jean

ideas.name: Test demand by listing before buying
ideas.one_liner: List items on Facebook Marketplace before you own them to measure clicks and messages as demand research.
ideas.problem: Resellers buy lots without knowing real demand
ideas.offer: A demand test using fake or pre-listings

pricing.notes: Chris listed Tesla wall chargers at $450-$500.

acquisition_channels.details: Pre-list on Facebook Marketplace and count clicks and messages.

ideas.delivery: Not a standalone business; research step before purchase.
unit_economics_claims: Tesla wall chargers cost about $600 landed, sold for $450-$500; could have sold 20

acquisition.how: Agents can draft test listings but posting needs human approval.

uk_applicability.notes: Works on UK Facebook Marketplace; note consumer-law implications of listing items you do not own.

risks: Listing items you do not own may be misleading or breach platform rules

quotes.text: That's something that almost no one thinks to do is to like list stuff before you have it just for the research purpose.
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: Free couch flipping
ideas.one_liner: Pick up free couches from Facebook Marketplace, clean and photograph them, resell for profit.
ideas.customer: Local furniture buyers, especially in college towns
ideas.problem: Cheap furniture demand; free couches abandoned

acquisition_channels.details: Sell on Facebook Marketplace from driveway.

ideas.delivery: Collect, clean in garage, photograph, sell from driveway.

uk_applicability.notes: Works in UK; fire-safety labelling rules apply to upholstered furniture sold in UK.

risks: Fire safety labels on UK upholstered furniture

quotes.text: picks up free couches from Facebook Marketplace, takes them home, cleans them up in his garage, takes better photos and everything, puts them back out in his driveway, and sells them
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: Flat-pack furniture truckload for college move-in
ideas.one_liner: Resell a truckload of new flat-pack furniture to parents of students in a college town before the semester.
ideas.problem: Students need cheap furniture at move-in

acquisition_channels.details: Facebook Marketplace and groups such as Flown and Grown.

uk_applicability.notes: UK university towns and Facebook groups work; timing is September.

quotes.text: you're right in between two colleges. And they're getting ready You know, it's July, so this is perfect timing to start talking to parents.
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: Overstock AA battery lot (GovDeals)
ideas.one_liner: Buy 8,000 long-shelf-life AA batteries at government auction and resell by the pack or wholesale.
ideas.customer: Online buyers (eBay/Amazon) and local discount retailers
ideas.offer: Brand new 10-year shelf life batteries at about $1 each

pricing.notes: Amazon retail packs about $2 per battery.

acquisition_channels.details: Sell on eBay and Amazon; wholesale to local shops by email and relationship.

ideas.delivery: Six to eight boxes; ship in free priority envelopes or hand over locally.

acquisition.how: Listings and wholesale emails to limited companies can be automated.

uk_applicability.notes: UK equivalents exist for public-sector auctions; battery sales trigger UK WEEE/battery producer obligations.

quotes.text: on the current versions they basically sell for about a buck a battery.
quotes.speaker: Shannon Jean

ideas.name: Costco liquidation resale in towns without a Costco
ideas.one_liner: Buy Costco liquidation pallets and sell in cities with no Costco (Waco, Jackson, Amarillo, etc.).
ideas.customer: Shoppers in mid-size cities without a Costco
ideas.problem: No local access to Costco goods
tools: ChatGPT to find cities with no Costco

uk_applicability.notes: UK has fewer Costcos; the concept (Costco/Costco-like store liquidations) is workable but needs UK sourcing.

quotes.text: you can buy Costco liquidation items and offer them in your local community that doesn't have a Costco.
quotes.speaker: Shannon Jean

ideas.name: IKEA pickup service for cities without IKEA
ideas.one_liner: Pre-collect orders, add 30%, drive to the nearest IKEA, then deliver in a parking-lot meetup.
ideas.customer: Shoppers in cities without an IKEA

acquisition_channels.details: Chris's guest ran 'My Modern South' in Huntsville; ordering via ikea.com carts.

ideas.delivery: Rent a U-Haul, drive to Atlanta or Memphis, deliver at a parking lot with a 2-hour window.
ideas.startup_cost: not stated; payment collected up front

uk_applicability.notes: UK has many IKEAs and strong delivery options, so the gap is smaller.

quotes.text: I would literally just say, "Go to ikea.com. Tell me what like fill your cart, print out your cart. I'm going to add 30% to it."
quotes.speaker: Shannon Jean

tactics.name: Reverse-engineer your bid
steps: List what you believe each item sells for
Subtract freight and costs to get a maximum bid
Place the max bid and walk away

tactics.name: Bid on weekends
steps: Costco auctions close on weekends and sell for less

tactics.name: Recover your investment first
steps: Identify high-ticket items in the manifest
Sell enough quickly to get money back
Wholesale part of the lot if needed

tactics.name: Wholesale to local discount stores
steps: Walk in without product and ask if they buy from resellers
Email manifest opportunities and let them name a price

tactics.name: Story-based listings
steps: Add your personal reason for selling

warnings.warning: Never buy without a manifest; you have no recourse.

quote.text: never buy a deal unless you're very sophisticated buyer without a manifest cuz you'll have no recourse.
quote.speaker: Shannon Jean

warnings.warning: Avoid hyped brands like Stanley where bids reflect retail; you can end up upside down.

quote.text: You can't pay 50% of what you find them in selling for. You'll be upside down on this deal.
quote.speaker: Shannon Jean

warnings.warning: Retail values on manifests are inflated.
Don't buy categories you don't know (car parts, Lego, consumer electronics).

lessons.lesson: Buy with math and sell with emotion.

quote.text: buy with math and sell with emotion because if you use emotion when you buy, the math never works.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Boring commodities have less competition than sexy products.
When starting, focus on getting your money back, not maximum profit.
Buy close to home to reduce freight.
Seasonal timing gives built-in downside protection.
Larger quantities of items reduce risk.

evidence_quality.rationale: Anecdotal, hypothetical profit math and second-hand claims from a promotional episode; live screen-share shows real listings but no verified outcomes.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Shannon Jean sells a Reseller Mastermind; Chris Koerner sells TK Owners and has a Beehiiv sponsor.
